clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse has opened a sterile drape and is placing a sterile instrument onto the field. Which placement maintains sterility according to NCBI Nursing Skills guidance?

options.A: Place the instrument more than 1 inch inside the edge of the sterile field.
options.B: Place the instrument on the outer 1-inch border when the drape remains dry.
options.C: Place the instrument on the sterile drape where it hangs below the tabletop.
options.D: Place the instrument on any area of the field after sterile gloves are donned.

semantic_correction.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills identifies any part of a sterile field within 1 inch of the edge as contaminated. It also identifies portions of the field that extend below the planar surface and areas below waist level or above shoulder level as contaminated. Therefore, a sterile instrument should be placed beyond the contaminated outer 1-inch border on the visible planar sterile field. Dryness or wearing sterile gloves does not convert a contaminated border or hanging portion into a sterile area.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Maintain a sterile field by treating the outer 1-inch border and any portion extending below the planar surface as contaminated.
semantic_correction.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf, Open RN
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Nursing Skills, 2nd edition (2023); current NCBI Bookshelf chapter accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Section 4.4 Sterile Fields — contaminated areas include any part within 1 inch of the edge, any part extending below the planar surface, and areas below waist level or above shoulder level
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: The outer 1 inch of a sterile field is considered contaminated; portions extending below the planar surface and specified out-of-view/position areas are also considered contaminated.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p. 24 — Apply principles of infection prevention; detailed printed p. 26 — Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions/Surgical Asepsis: use appropriate technique to set up a sterile field and maintain asepsis

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: converted the recall wording into a bedside sterile-instrument placement decision, removed the 'only' distractor pattern, and used adjacent sterile-field contamination principles as plausible alternatives.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed pp. 24 and 26
audit_findings_append.finding: The source directly supports the 1-inch contaminated border. The revised item tests application of that rule rather than simple restatement and uses realistic sterile-field positioning distractors.

option_audit.A: Correct. Placement more than 1 inch inside the edge avoids the contaminated border described by the source.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. The outer 1-inch border remains contaminated even when the drape is dry.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Any portion extending below the planar surface is considered contaminated.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Sterile gloves do not make every area of the field sterile; location-based contamination rules still apply.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A is the only placement that avoids both the explicitly contaminated outer border and other contaminated field locations.
cueing_check: All four options are sterile-instrument placement decisions of comparable length and structure; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
